# Glimow Studio

Glimow Studio

Glimow Studio develops FlameSight, an AI-driven camera network designed to detect wildfire ignition points in real time. The product integrates with existing utility vegetation management systems to provide early alerts on potential fire outbreaks near power lines and critical infrastructure.

Product Overview

FlameSight combines high-resolution thermal and optical cameras with advanced machine learning algorithms to monitor fire-prone areas continuously. Key features include:

- Real-time detection of smoke plumes and heat signatures
- Automated alerts sent directly to utility control centers
- Integration with outage risk assessment tools
- Adaptive learning to reduce false positives in diverse environmental conditions

Customers and Use Cases

FlameSight primarily serves utility companies responsible for vegetation management along transmission and distribution lines. Current deployments focus on regions with intense wildfire risk during dry seasons. Notable customers include the Pacific Northwest Electric Cooperative and Central Ridge Power Authority, which use FlameSight to prioritize line inspections and expedite outage response.

Company Stage and Traction

Founded in 2021, Glimow Studio has raised $7.5 million in seed and Series A funding led by Horizon Ventures and Greenline Capital. FlameSight is deployed across 12 regional power grids, collectively covering over 150,000 square kilometers. Early adopters report a 40% reduction in wildfire response times, leading to fewer outages and lower firefighting costs.

Team

The founding team includes CEO Dana Ryu, formerly a wildfire risk analyst; CTO Victor Salinas, a computer vision expert; and Chief Product Officer Leila Kim, specializing in utility software integrations. The company employs 28 engineers and data scientists based in Boulder, Colorado.

Competitive Landscape

Key competitors in the wildfire detection space include EmberGuard Systems, FireNet Analytics, and PyraVision Technologies. While many competitors focus on satellite or drone-based detection, FlameSight’s fixed camera network offers continuous, localized monitoring with superior real-time responsiveness.

Open Risks

- Environmental variability causing occasional false alarms
- Dependence on utility customers’ willingness to integrate new technologies
- Scalability challenges in deploying cameras over extremely remote terrain
- Potential regulatory changes affecting camera surveillance deployments

Glimow Studio continues to refine FlameSight’s AI models and expand its network partnerships to address these risks and strengthen its market position.
